facts.label: Conflicts and version relationships
facts.text: - Acquisition price: the annual report states "purchase consideration of $2,642.7 million, net of cash acquired" (page:79); the latest quarterly report states "purchase consideration of $2,637.7 million, net of cash acquired" (page:5) after a recorded "purchase price refund". (page:99). The latest quarterly report records later events through October 21, 2026, including "an Order reversing and vacating the Judgment" (page:13), and notes the plaintiffs may seek further review. The latest filing controls; the earlier one remains the record as of its date. - Debt table versions: the December 2025, March 2026 and September 2026 quarterly debt tables and the annual table are each retained as separate dated sources. A search of that release for calendar year and transition found nothing. Whether the stated guidance still covers a year ending June 2027 or the transition period is unresolved. This is a conflict of basis, not of figures. - Release versus filing: release non-GAAP measures (EBITDA, adjusted net income, free cash flow excluding the receivables sale program) are management claims. They do not override the statements.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for statement-based credit work, with restrictions. The audited FY2026 and FY2025 statements, three quarterly filings and three releases give a consistent consolidated base in USD. On printed inputs, total debt (principal) over management EBITDA was 3.04x at FY2025, 4.20x at FY2026 and 3.94x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt over EBITDA was 2.93x, 4.04x and 3.72x. EBITDA over cash interest paid was 6.67x, 5.49x and 5.60x. Leverage rose because the March 2026 acquisition was financed with new term debt and add-on notes while its earnings entered the base only from March 9, 2026; the latest twelve-month ratio therefore still carries a part-year earnings contribution against the full acquisition debt balance, and no pro forma figure is supplied. The restrictions are: EBITDA is management defined and unadjusted for stock compensation and acquisition costs; covenant definitions and levels are Not supplied, so no covenant ratio or headroom is computed; a fiscal-year change makes the next report a six-month transition period; and obligations outside the debt figure (operating leases, the receivable sale program, supplemental retirement obligations, contingent consideration) are listed but not added to leverage.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Management EBITDA: net income plus income taxes, net interest income and expense, and depreciation and amortisation including depreciation within direct costs (Q1 FY2027 release page:10). The four published reconciliations were re-added and tie to the printed totals (see Calculations). Stock-based compensation (79.514 in FY2026, cash flow statement) is not added back, and the Q3 FY2026 release states EBITDA "includes $17.4 million of ARKA-related transaction expenses" (Q3 release page:1). No adjusted EBITDA is reported; the company reports adjusted net income only. - Interest: "Interest expense and other, net" is one line. Cash interest is the cash flow supplemental line. Neither is a covenant interest measure. - Total debt here is principal of the six listed instruments. Operating leases, receivable sales, retirement obligations, contingent consideration and the swaps are outside it. - Covenant definitions: the only text names "a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio" (10-Q ended December 31, 2025, page:12) and later filings state compliance. Levels, step-downs, definitions and the reported ratios are Not supplied. The metrics above are not the covenant metrics.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, credit implication
facts.text: Leverage. Evidence: principal debt rose from 2,942.625 to 4,931.125 between June 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (10-K page:86) while management EBITDA rose from 966.796 to 1,173.914 (release page:12). Mechanism: the acquisition debt arrived in March 2026 and its earnings are in the base for under four months of FY2026 and for under seven months of the latest twelve months, so reported ratios carry a timing mismatch that may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of that effect is not supplied because no pro forma figure is given (the 10-K states pro forma results were not material, page:81). Implication: reported leverage of 3.94x on the latest twelve months may overstate run-rate leverage, and should be refined when later periods carry more of the acquired earnings or a pro forma figure is supplied.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, credit implication
facts.text: Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash 279.389 and undrawn revolver 1,395.0 at September 30, 2026 against 46.750 scheduled in FY2027 and no maturity above 78.000 until FY2031. Mechanism: the revolver matures November 2030 and carries a 605.000 drawn balance, so refinancing risk sits in FY2031 and beyond; the receivable sale program (sold balance at the 350.0 maximum) expires in December 2026 and is a short-dated source of working-capital cash outside the debt figure. Implication: near-term liquidity is not a constraint on printed inputs; renewal of the receivable program is the nearest dated funding event.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CACI is a Delaware holding company whose operating subsidiaries provide technology and expertise to national security customers, with essentially all revenue from the U.S. federal government. The view for a creditor is that business risk is dominated by funding and contract-structure mechanics rather than by market competition: revenue visibility comes from a large backlog but depends on annual appropriations and on contracts that the government may terminate for convenience; margin resilience depends on the contract mix, which moved toward fixed-price work in the latest quarter; and cash conversion depends on receivable collection and on a receivable sale program that is nearly at its cap and has a stated term ending in December 2026. The one transformative transaction in the record is the March 2026 acquisition of a space-domain technology business, financed with an 800.0 million term loan tranche, a 500.0 million add-on of senior unsecured notes and revolver borrowings, after which the revolver balance has fallen. Ownership is public and dispersed on the evidence supplied, but control rights and holder concentration are Not supplied because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and is not in the pack. No sponsor behaviour can be assessed because none is named. The record shows no dividend ever paid and sharply reduced share repurchases in FY2026. The fiscal-year change disclosed on October 20, 2026 and the October 2026 court developments are subsequent events and are kept out of FY2026 facts.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The principal transaction is the acquisition of ARKA Group L.P., which closed on March 9, 2026 under a purchase agreement and plan of merger dated December 19, 2025, among a CACI operating subsidiary, the issuer, a merger subsidiary, the target and two other limited partnerships (10-K exhibit index, page:104). The 10-K states purchase consideration of 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, subject to post-closing adjustments, that the acquisition is intended to enhance the ability to deliver advanced technology for national security customers in the space domain, and that it was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand (10-K page:79). The allocation recorded 1,145.0 million of intangible assets and 1,462.9 million of goodwill (10-K page:80). The target's sellers, any sponsor or minority interest and any earnout are not described in the supplied text, which is an Insufficient Information item. A smaller acquisition of a data and cloud migration business by the U.K. subsidiary closed on February 17, 2026 for 10.7 million net of cash acquired (10-K page:81). Management reports post-acquisition revenue of 166.8 million and net income of 17.4 million for the two businesses together in FY2026, after 26.0 million of intangible amortisation (10-K page:81); this is a partial-period contribution and not a run-rate figure. In the latest quarter the consideration was reduced to 2,637.7 million after a 5.0 million purchase price refund from the final working capital settlement, and the allocation is still preliminary (Q1 10-Q page:5). The two figures are logged as a conflict of versions below and are not reconciled here.

facts.text: New debt linked to the transaction. On March 9, 2026 the company amended its Term Loan B agreement to add a 800.0 million seven-year senior secured Term Loan B-2 (10-K page:88, page:89). On March 12, 2026 it issued an additional 500.0 million of its 6.375% senior unsecured notes due June 2033, forming part of the same series as the 1,000.0 million notes issued on June 2, 2025, at a premium, with net proceeds of 516.5 million used to repay revolver borrowings (10-K page:89). A senior secured bridge loan commitment of up to 1,300.0 million dated December 19, 2025 was never drawn and was terminated on March 9, 2026 (10-K page:81). Earlier and related financing events: the Term Loan B of 750.0 million on October 30, 2024; the 1,000.0 million notes of June 2, 2025, whose net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings; and the November 25, 2025 amendment of the senior secured credit facility, made primarily to extend its maturity (10-K page:88, page:89). Revolver borrowings also funded part of the price: the revolver was drawn 928.0 million at March 31, 2026 and 605.0 million at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 base). facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience, backlog of 34.0 billion of which 6.2 billion is funded (10-K page:12, page:8; Q1 10-Q page:20). Mechanic: appropriations, continuing resolutions and option exercise determine conversion of backlog to cash; a lapse in funding delays awards and collections for all agencies at once. Implication: revenue is durable in normal budget conditions but its stress case is a funding disruption, not competition; the nearest dated exposure is the continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026. Countering item: a book-to-bill of 2.0x in the latest quarter, although contract awards were below the prior-year quarter (Q1 FY2027 release pages:1, 9). 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share up from 26.7% to 33.2% and cost-plus-fee down from 60.5% to 52.8% between Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 (Q1 FY2027 release page:8). Mechanic: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Implication: earnings and cash flow become more variable with execution; this is a year-over-year change in one quarter, and a counter-signal is the higher EBITDA margin reported for Q1 FY2027 in the CP-1 base. 3. Acquisition and leverage mechanics. Evidence: 2,642.7 million consideration funded by borrowings, 800.0 million term loan, 500.0 million notes (10-K pages:79, 88, 89). Mechanic: debt arrived before a full period of acquired earnings, so reported leverage in the CP-1 base is not a run-rate figure. Implication: deleveraging depends on cash flow after interest and on future acquisition appetite; conflicts logged above affect the price but not the financing amounts. 4. Concentration. Evidence: Department of War 53.6% of FY2026 revenue and ten contracts at 22.5% (10-K page:12, page:8). Mechanic: agency-specific budget decisions and re-competes. Implication: moderate contract concentration, high payer concentration. 5. Key uncertainties. Covenant levels, guarantors, ownership and control rights, acquired earnings, the effect of the fiscal-year change, and the renewal of the receivable sale program.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: CACI's fundamental credit profile is sound but more leveraged after its March 2026 acquisition, resting on a federally funded business that converts earnings into cash. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 against scheduled debt maturities of USD 46.750 million in FY2027, with EBITDA covering cash interest 5.60x over the twelve months to that date. The weakest point is leverage of 3.94x total debt to EBITDA, in a business that relies on one payer and on government funding and termination conditions. The outcome depends on deleveraging from cash flow while federal funding stays orderly; covenant terms and guarantors are not disclosed in the supplied sources and remain unverified.

citations.quote: CACI's fundamental credit profile is sound but more leveraged after its March 2026 acquisition, resting on a federally funded business that converts earnings into cash. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 against scheduled debt maturities of USD 46.750 million in FY2027, with EBITDA covering cash interest 5.60x over the twelve months to that date. The weakest point is leverage of 3.94x total debt to EBITDA, in a business that relies on one payer and on government funding and termination conditions. The outcome depends on deleveraging from cash flow while federal funding stays orderly; covenant terms and guarantors are not disclosed in the supplied sources and remain unverified.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. CACI's leverage stepped up with the March 2026 acquisition and has only partly eased. Total debt to EBITDA was 3.04x at FY2025, 4.20x at FY2026 and 3.94x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 2.93x, 4.04x and 3.72x [CP-1 financial base]. The acquired business entered earnings for under seven months of that latest period while its financing is fully in debt, so the reported ratio may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of the effect is Not supplied because no pro forma earnings are given [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary]. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, revenue is almost entirely federal and backlog-supported, which gives revenue visibility in normal budget conditions [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Second, liquidity is ample: cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,674.389 million against light scheduled amortisation [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Third, cash generation is solid, with operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 775.961 million and cash interest cover of 5.60x on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-supportive on the record: no dividend has been paid, share repurchases were cut and the revolver balance fell from USD 660.0 million to USD 605.0 million in the latest quarter [CP-1A governance table] (Documentary Fact). Fifth, the margin trend is positive, with management EBITDA margin of 13.3% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 11.7% a year earlier [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Management describes its execution as a differentiator, which is Management Language and is not adopted here [CP-1A company and operating model] (Management Language).

spans.text: ## Request

Module: source readiness for CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ (issuer id caci, ticker CACI). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot, run type research, public case. Reporting currency named by the context: USD. Context periods: current period fiscal first quarter of FY2027 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), prior period FY2026 (year ended June 30, 2026).

Question answered here: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream work (the selected minimum module set CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and the report sections key findings, company operating model, model chart strip, financials and credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile, transaction summary), and what stays blocked. This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalise, reconcile or calculate figures. The assertion for the HTML model objective is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.
The user context holds dated settings only. It is not issuer evidence. It leaves blank the ratings, quotes, deal terms, peer and market inputs, and these are not treated as zero.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
Locators below use the form file name plus the source chunk shown as page:N, which is not the printed page.
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
User context (settings, not issuer evidence): context sha256 771458f144b8d7a95d0c8ef74d2f2b133b5846c23aea051905b07e94014f45fd.
### Handoffs supplied
None. CP-0 is the first module in this run, so CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff. No handoff is relied on, and none is corrected here.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filed statements and earnings releases are sufficient for downstream financial, business and transaction work with stated limits. The legal debt documents are absent, so covenant levels and guarantors cannot be sourced. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or subsidiary list is supplied, so covenant levels, headroom and the guarantor group stay unsourced. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited annual statements and three quarterly filings cover the issuer consolidated perimeter, with the latest quarter ended September 30, 2026. | Statement-based debt, liquidity, cash flow and earnings work can proceed from filed evidence. | High |
| Covenant types are named once, but no level, step-down or reported ratio is supplied. | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed from this pack; only compliance statements are available. | High |

| The board approved a change to a calendar fiscal year after the last quarter, creating a six-month transition period. | Period labels and the basis of management fiscal year guidance need care in later work. | Medium |

| The legal matter and the acquisition accounting are updated in the latest quarterly filing. | Later filings supersede the annual filing on these facts, so downstream modules must prefer the latest filing. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for every selected consumer. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. The set holds one audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases, all filed by the same registrant, with text extracted for every source and no source-level preparation block. Readiness here means source sufficiency only, not completion of any downstream analysis, and a successful text extraction is not a fidelity review of tables. The limitations that travel with every consumer are: no executed debt documents, so covenant levels, definitions, guarantors and baskets are not sourced; no investor presentations, only releases; the gap in quarterly releases and balance sheets listed in Gaps; and the fiscal-year change disclosed after the last quarter.
| Consumer | Source view | Evidence it demands | Limitations carried |

| CP-1 financial data | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt note, liquidity, cash paid for interest and tax, segment and revenue tables, non-GAAP reconciliations | Debt table gives principal by facility but unamortised discount only in total; covenant levels not supplied; no balance sheet at the first quarter of the prior fiscal year |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, acquisition notes, legal proceedings, customer and contract mix, management narrative in releases | Merger agreement and financing commitment documents are listed in the exhibit index but not supplied; management statements are attributed claims; ownership is public with no sponsor named in the context |
| CP-2 credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Settled upstream registers only | Inherits all limitations of the upstream modules; planner sequencing, not source readiness, governs this |

| CP-5 evidence trace | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Pinned pack for quote matching and cross-module identity | Where a later filing updates an earlier one, both are retained and the later controls the later date |
### Source assessment

Each row names document family, original authority, entity and perimeter, period and basis, a located quote, and the limits. Filed statements carry authority for their facts; releases give attributed management claims and non-GAAP measures; neither overrides a filing.
| Source | Family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Located evidence | Limits |

| 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K; filed statements with an audit opinion; controls for annual facts | Registrant CACI International Inc, a holding company; consolidated with subsidiaries | Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), with FY2025 and FY2024 comparatives; USD thousands | "For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026" (page:1); "is a holding company whose operations are conducted through subsidiaries primarily located in the U.S. and Europe" (page:5) | Parent-only statements not supplied; the exhibit list marks subsidiaries as filed but the list is not in the pack |

| 10-Q_2025-12-31_caci-20251231.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q; unaudited | Consolidated, before the large March 2026 acquisition | Quarter and six months ended December 31, 2025 (FY2026 second quarter); balance sheet against June 30, 2025 | "For the quarterly period ended December 31, 2025" (page:1) | Only source naming covenant types; its debt table has no acquisition-related tranches |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_caci-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q; unaudited | Consolidated, including the acquisition closed in the quarter | Quarter and nine months ended March 31, 2026 (FY2026 third quarter) | "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026" (page:1) | Acquisition allocation preliminary at that date |

| EX-99.1_2026-04-22_fy26-q3caci20260422ex991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release exhibit; management presentation of results | CACI International Inc consolidated | FY2026 third quarter and nine months; includes non-GAAP EBITDA, adjusted income and free cash flow | "EBITDA of $289.7 million" (page:1) | Attributed management claims; non-GAAP; not a filing of record for audited facts |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-05_fy26-q4caci20260805ex991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release exhibit; fiscal year 2027 guidance issued | Consolidated | FY2026 fourth quarter and twelve months; guidance for FY2027 | "Annual EBITDA of $1,173.9 million and EBITDA margin of 12.3%" (page:1) | Only source with discrete fourth-quarter statements of operations (page:8); guidance is a forecast |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl | Earnings release exhibit; guidance raised | Consolidated | FY2027 first quarter ended September 30, 2026 | "EBITDA of $328.8 million and EBITDA margin of 13.3%" (page:1) | Does not mention the calendar-year change; guidance basis unresolved |
### Perimeter and entity roles

- Issuer and registrant: CACI International Inc, a Delaware corporation and holding company ("The term “the Registrant” refers to CACI International Inc only." page:5 of the annual report). The context names the issuer as CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ with no borrower, parent, guarantor or sponsor entered. The filings carry the same commission file number 001-31400, so identity across the seven sources is consistent.

- Statements are consolidated. The debt note states the senior secured credit facility, term loans and senior unsecured notes at the issuer level, and the amended credit facility agreement lists subsidiaries and a lender group in the exhibit index only ("Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement" page:104 of the annual report).
- Guarantors: the indenture exhibits state "the guarantors named therein" (page:104) but no source supplied here names them. This is an unresolved distinction, not a zero.
- Restricted or unrestricted subsidiary status: Not supplied; no source defines it.
- Segments: Domestic Operations and International Operations; the annual report states the international share of revenue in the business section (page:7).

- Receivables sale: a separate Master Accounts Receivable Purchase Agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd. as purchaser, off the debt table ("up to a maximum amount of $350.0 million", annual report page:85; the later filing repeats it on page:8). The annual note states the term was extended to "December 18, 2026" (page:85), a contract date after the cutoff, labelled as a term, not an event.
### Coverage against the requested objective

Discrete quarters, fiscal years, quarter versus year-to-date, segments, add-backs, KPIs, facility-level debt, cash-paid interest and tax, and the business narrative were each searched for. Located evidence:
| Item | Located evidence | Status |
| Fiscal years | Statements of operations, balance sheets and cash flows with three fiscal years of income and cash flow, two balance sheets (annual report page:65 to page:67) | Retained |
| Latest quarter against prior-year quarter | "Revenues $ 2,474,597 $ 2,287,623" (10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:2) | Retained |
| Second and third fiscal quarters with year-to-date | Three-month and six or nine-month columns (10-Q ended December 31, 2025, page:2; 10-Q ended March 31, 2026, page:2) | Retained |

| Fourth fiscal quarter | Three-month columns in the release ("EBITDA $ 353,064 $ 264,538 33.5% $ 1,173,914 $ 966,796 21.4%", fourth-quarter release page:12) | Retained for the release measures; the annual report holds no discrete quarter |

| Segments | "Domestic Operations and International Operations" with revenue, costs, depreciation and income from operations (annual report page:98; 10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:12) | Retained |

| Add-backs and non-GAAP | Reconciliations of net income to adjusted net income and to EBITDA ("EBITDA $ 328,828 $ 268,613", first-quarter release page:10) | Retained as management measures, with management definitions |
| KPIs | Backlog, awards, book-to-bill, days sales outstanding, revenue by customer and contract type (first-quarter release page:1, page:4, page:8, page:9) | Retained |

| Facility-level debt | Principal, rate, maturity by facility ("Principal amount of long-term debt 4,864,438 4,931,125", 10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:9) | Retained for principal; carrying value net of discount is given only as one total |

| Cash-paid interest and tax | "Cash paid during the period for interest" and for income taxes (annual report page:67; 10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:4) | Retained for the year, for the six months, nine months and latest quarter (10-Q ended December 31, 2025 and 10-Q ended March 31, 2026, page:4); discrete second and third quarter values would need derivation downstream |
| Liquidity | "$1,395.0 million of undrawn capacity under the Revolving Facility" (10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:21) | Retained |
| Business and transaction narrative | Business section, acquisition notes, legal note (annual report page:5 to page:9, page:79 to page:81, page:99) | Retained |

Presentations: no investor presentation is in the pack, so no slide coverage is claimed. The first-quarter release says slide exhibits accompany the call, and they are not supplied. Releases are text only; no image or chart content was inspected.
### Conflicts and version relationships

- Acquisition price: the annual report states "purchase consideration of $2,642.7 million, net of cash acquired" (page:79); the latest quarterly report states "purchase consideration of $2,637.7 million, net of cash acquired" (page:5) after a recorded "purchase price refund". Both are retained; the later filing controls for the later date. The allocation remains preliminary in both ("has not finalized the determination of fair values", latest quarterly report page:5).

- Legal matter: the annual report states the Court of Appeals matter was still before the court and "No amounts have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements." (page:99). The latest quarterly report records later events through October 21, 2026, including "an Order reversing and vacating the Judgment" (page:13), and notes the plaintiffs may seek further review. The latest filing controls; the earlier one remains the record as of its date.

- Debt table versions: the December 2025, March 2026 and September 2026 quarterly debt tables and the annual table are each retained as separate dated sources. They are not collapsed; later tranches (a second term loan tranche and an add-on of senior notes) appear only from the March 2026 report.

- Period basis: the first-quarter release states fiscal year 2027 guidance with no reference to the calendar-year change that the quarterly report discloses ("approved changing the Company’s fiscal year to a calendar year", page:13). A search of that release for calendar year and transition found nothing. Whether the stated guidance still covers a year ending June 2027 or the transition period is unresolved. This is a conflict of basis, not of figures.
- Release versus filing: release non-GAAP measures (EBITDA, adjusted net income, free cash flow excluding the receivables sale program) are management claims. They do not override the statements.
### Analytical read-through

Usable coverage. Evidence: a full set of filed statements for the year ended June 30, 2026 and three quarters, plus the debt note listing each facility ("Revolving Facility November 2030", annual report page:86). Mechanism: facility-level principal, rate, maturity and amortisation can be read directly, so maturity and liquidity work does not depend on estimation. Consequence: financial, liquidity and transaction modules can proceed from filed evidence.

Strongest contrary evidence. The only text on covenant tests is generic: "including a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio" (10-Q ended December 31, 2025, page:12), and later filings state only compliance ("in compliance with all of its financial covenants related to all long-term debt", 10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:9). Mechanism: with no executed credit agreement, no level, definition or step-down can be located, and management compliance statements are attributed assertions. Consequence: any covenant headroom, definition difference or cushion analysis cannot proceed; downstream modules must write the gap, not an estimate.

Structure. Evidence: "A majority of our assets serve as collateral under the Credit Facility." (annual report page:88) and senior unsecured notes described as "subordinated to existing senior secured indebtedness" (page:89). Mechanism: ranking and collateral are described in prose without guarantor names or collateral schedule; the wording on the notes is quoted as printed and not reinterpreted. Consequence: recovery and structural-ranking work is limited to the prose descriptions.

Period change. Evidence: the transition-period note (10-Q ended September 30, 2026, page:13). Mechanism: the next report will cover six months, not a quarter, so a year-over-year quarter comparison will not be available from the next filing. Consequence: later modules must label every figure by period and must not mix a three-month, six-month or twelve-month amount.

Next evidence action: obtain the credit agreement and its amendments, the indentures, the subsidiary list and the guarantor schedule, and, if discrete quarterly history is wanted, the second-quarter FY2026 release and the balance sheet at the end of the first quarter of FY2026.
## Calculations

No new calculation is made in this module. The method for source readiness forbids normalising, reconciling or computing figures. Every figure quoted above is a verbatim substring of a retained source span. Covenant headroom, net debt, leverage, liquidity and growth rates are Not calculable here because they are downstream work and, for covenant headroom, because the covenant levels are not supplied.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation | Citation or basis |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for statement-based credit work, with restrictions. The audited FY2026 and FY2025 statements, three quarterly filings and three releases give a consistent consolidated base in USD. EBITDA over cash interest paid was 6.67x, 5.49x and 5.60x. Leverage rose because the March 2026 acquisition was financed with new term debt and add-on notes while its earnings entered the base only from March 9, 2026; the latest twelve-month ratio therefore still carries a part-year earnings contribution against the full acquisition debt balance, and no pro forma figure is supplied. The restrictions are: EBITDA is management defined and unadjusted for stock compensation and acquisition costs; covenant definitions and levels are Not supplied, so no covenant ratio or headroom is computed; a fiscal-year change makes the next report a six-month transition period; and obligations outside the debt figure (operating leases, the receivable sale program, supplemental retirement obligations, contingent consideration) are listed but not added to leverage.

### Definition review

### Latest quarter and subsequent events

- Quarter ended September 30, 2026: revenues up 8.2% with organic growth of 2.1% (Q1 10-Q page:18); a 5.0 purchase-price refund reduced the ARKA consideration to 2,637.7 and moved the cash flow acquisitions line to a positive 5.0 (10-Q pages:3, 5).

- Subsequent to the balance sheet: the Board approved on October 20, 2026 a change to a calendar fiscal year with a six-month transition period to December 31, 2026 (10-Q page:13); the Court of Appeals issued the mandate on October 20 and the District Court vacated the judgment on October 21, 2026 (10-Q page:13); fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on October 21, 2026 (release page:4); the receivable sale program term ends December 18, 2026 (10-K page:85, after the cutoff and stated here as a contract term only).

- Financing events in FY2026: Credit Facility amended November 25, 2025 to extend maturity; Term Loan B-2 of 800.0 on March 9, 2026; 500.0 add-on notes on March 12, 2026 with 516.5 net proceeds; a 1,300.0 bridge commitment was undrawn and terminated March 9, 2026 (10-K pages:81, 88, 89). Swaps of 800.0 were added in May 2026 (10-K page:90).
### Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, credit implication

Leverage. Evidence: principal debt rose from 2,942.625 to 4,931.125 between June 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (10-K page:86) while management EBITDA rose from 966.796 to 1,173.914 (release page:12). Mechanism: the acquisition debt arrived in March 2026 and its earnings are in the base for under four months of FY2026 and for under seven months of the latest twelve months, so reported ratios carry a timing mismatch that may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of that effect is not supplied because no pro forma figure is given (the 10-K states pro forma results were not material, page:81). Implication: reported leverage of 3.94x on the latest twelve months may overstate run-rate leverage, and should be refined when later periods carry more of the acquired earnings or a pro forma figure is supplied.

Coverage and cash. Evidence: cash interest paid 213.640 in FY2026 and 42.619 in Q1 FY2027 against an income statement charge of 215.454 and 73.240. Mechanism: the quarterly cash number omits note coupons (semi-annual) and floating-rate timing; the income statement charge is the better guide to the current interest run-rate. Implication: do not annualise the Q1 FY2027 cash interest; the cover ratios in the charts are historical cash-basis cover.

Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash 279.389 and undrawn revolver 1,395.0 at September 30, 2026 against 46.750 scheduled in FY2027 and no maturity above 78.000 until FY2031. Mechanism: the revolver matures November 2030 and carries a 605.000 drawn balance, so refinancing risk sits in FY2031 and beyond; the receivable sale program (sold balance at the 350.0 maximum) expires in December 2026 and is a short-dated source of working-capital cash outside the debt figure. Implication: near-term liquidity is not a constraint on printed inputs; renewal of the receivable program is the nearest dated funding event.

Interest rate exposure. Evidence: floating-rate instruments total 3,364.438 (revolver, Term Loan, Term Loan B, Term Loan B-2) against swaps of 1,400.0 notional, and management states a one percent move changes quarterly interest on variable debt by 5.1 (10-Q page:22). Mechanism: about 1,964.438 of floating debt is unhedged by the notional shown, and swaps mature through 2030. Implication: higher rates would raise cash interest and reduce cover.

### Business and transaction view

CACI is a Delaware holding company whose operating subsidiaries provide technology and expertise to national security customers, with essentially all revenue from the U.S. federal government. The view for a creditor is that business risk is dominated by funding and contract-structure mechanics rather than by market competition: revenue visibility comes from a large backlog but depends on annual appropriations and on contracts that the government may terminate for convenience; margin resilience depends on the contract mix, which moved toward fixed-price work in the latest quarter; and cash conversion depends on receivable collection and on a receivable sale program that is nearly at its cap and has a stated term ending in December 2026. The one transformative transaction in the record is the March 2026 acquisition of a space-domain technology business, financed with an 800.0 million term loan tranche, a 500.0 million add-on of senior unsecured notes and revolver borrowings, after which the revolver balance has fallen. Ownership is public and dispersed on the evidence supplied, but control rights and holder concentration are Not supplied because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and is not in the pack. No sponsor behaviour can be assessed because none is named. The record shows no dividend ever paid and sharply reduced share repurchases in FY2026. The fiscal-year change disclosed on October 20, 2026 and the October 2026 court developments are subsequent events and are kept out of FY2026 facts.

| Contract concentration | Ten largest contracts were 22.5% of FY2026 revenue | Documentary Fact | "accounted for 22.5% of our revenues, or $2.2 billion" (10-K page:8) | Loss or re-compete of a top contract could move earnings, but no single contract is dominant |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The principal transaction is the acquisition of ARKA Group L.P., which closed on March 9, 2026 under a purchase agreement and plan of merger dated December 19, 2025, among a CACI operating subsidiary, the issuer, a merger subsidiary, the target and two other limited partnerships (10-K exhibit index, page:104). The 10-K states purchase consideration of 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, subject to post-closing adjustments, that the acquisition is intended to enhance the ability to deliver advanced technology for national security customers in the space domain, and that it was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand (10-K page:79). The allocation recorded 1,145.0 million of intangible assets and 1,462.9 million of goodwill (10-K page:80). The target's sellers, any sponsor or minority interest and any earnout are not described in the supplied text, which is an Insufficient Information item. A smaller acquisition of a data and cloud migration business by the U.K. subsidiary closed on February 17, 2026 for 10.7 million net of cash acquired (10-K page:81). Management reports post-acquisition revenue of 166.8 million and net income of 17.4 million for the two businesses together in FY2026, after 26.0 million of intangible amortisation (10-K page:81); this is a partial-period contribution and not a run-rate figure. In the latest quarter the consideration was reduced to 2,637.7 million after a 5.0 million purchase price refund from the final working capital settlement, and the allocation is still preliminary (Q1 10-Q page:5). The two figures are logged as a conflict of versions below and are not reconciled here.

New debt linked to the transaction. On March 9, 2026 the company amended its Term Loan B agreement to add a 800.0 million seven-year senior secured Term Loan B-2 (10-K page:88, page:89). On March 12, 2026 it issued an additional 500.0 million of its 6.375% senior unsecured notes due June 2033, forming part of the same series as the 1,000.0 million notes issued on June 2, 2025, at a premium, with net proceeds of 516.5 million used to repay revolver borrowings (10-K page:89). Status and subsequent events. The acquisition is closed; the allocation is preliminary; the purchase agreement text, the credit agreement amendments and the indenture supplements are named in the exhibit index but are not supplied, so conditions, guarantors and covenants for the new debt are Not supplied. The fiscal-year change (October 20, 2026), the vacated judgment (October 21, 2026), the raised guidance (October 21, 2026) and the receivable program term ending December 18, 2026 are subsequent events or future contract terms, not FY2026 facts.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience, backlog of 34.0 billion of which 6.2 billion is funded (10-K page:12, page:8; Q1 10-Q page:20). Mechanic: appropriations, continuing resolutions and option exercise determine conversion of backlog to cash; a lapse in funding delays awards and collections for all agencies at once. Implication: revenue is durable in normal budget conditions but its stress case is a funding disruption, not competition; the nearest dated exposure is the continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026. Countering item: a book-to-bill of 2.0x in the latest quarter, although contract awards were below the prior-year quarter (Q1 FY2027 release pages:1, 9).

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share up from 26.7% to 33.2% and cost-plus-fee down from 60.5% to 52.8% between Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 (Q1 FY2027 release page:8). Mechanic: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Implication: earnings and cash flow become more variable with execution; this is a year-over-year change in one quarter, and a counter-signal is the higher EBITDA margin reported for Q1 FY2027 in the CP-1 base.

3. Acquisition and leverage mechanics. Evidence: 2,642.7 million consideration funded by borrowings, 800.0 million term loan, 500.0 million notes (10-K pages:79, 88, 89). Mechanic: debt arrived before a full period of acquired earnings, so reported leverage in the CP-1 base is not a run-rate figure. Implication: deleveraging depends on cash flow after interest and on future acquisition appetite; conflicts logged above affect the price but not the financing amounts.

4. Concentration. Evidence: Department of War 53.6% of FY2026 revenue and ten contracts at 22.5% (10-K page:12, page:8). Mechanic: agency-specific budget decisions and re-competes. Implication: moderate contract concentration, high payer concentration.
5. Key uncertainties. Covenant levels, guarantors, ownership and control rights, acquired earnings, the effect of the fiscal-year change, and the renewal of the receivable sale program.

### Credit view

CACI's fundamental credit profile is sound but more leveraged after its March 2026 acquisition, resting on a federally funded business that converts earnings into cash. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 against scheduled debt maturities of USD 46.750 million in FY2027, with EBITDA covering cash interest 5.60x over the twelve months to that date. The weakest point is leverage of 3.94x total debt to EBITDA, in a business that relies on one payer and on government funding and termination conditions. The outcome depends on deleveraging from cash flow while federal funding stays orderly; covenant terms and guarantors are not disclosed in the supplied sources and remain unverified.
### Key findings

1. CACI's leverage stepped up with the March 2026 acquisition and has only partly eased. Total debt to EBITDA was 3.04x at FY2025, 4.20x at FY2026 and 3.94x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 2.93x, 4.04x and 3.72x [CP-1 financial base]. The acquired business entered earnings for under seven months of that latest period while its financing is fully in debt, so the reported ratio may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of the effect is Not supplied because no pro forma earnings are given [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary]. Credit implication: leverage tolerance is the main variable, and it improves only if cash flow after interest is applied to debt.

2. CACI's liquidity is strong and its near-term maturity profile is light. Cash was USD 279.389 million and the undrawn revolver USD 1,395.0 million at September 30, 2026; scheduled maturities are USD 46.750 million in FY2027 and no more than USD 78.000 million a year until FY2031, when USD 1,706.750 million falls due, with USD 2,959.250 million after that [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: refinancing risk sits in FY2031 and beyond, and the revolver matures in November 2030. The receivable sale program is close to its USD 350.0 million cap and its stated term ends on December 18, 2026, so it should not be counted as spare liquidity [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary].

3. CACI's cash generation covers its interest comfortably on a historical basis. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.67x in FY2025, 5.49x in FY2026 and 5.60x on the latest twelve months, and operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 775.961 million on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base]. The quarterly cash interest figure omits semi-annual note coupons, and the income statement interest charge for the latest quarter exceeds cash paid, so the historical cover will not hold if the interest run-rate stays at the higher level [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate but the cushion has narrowed since FY2025.

4. CACI depends on a single payer, which concentrates funding and contract risk. Federal customers were 95.6% of FY2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6%, and the ten largest contracts 22.5%; the government may terminate contracts for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the government fiscal year only through December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1A timeline]. Credit implication: revenue visibility from the USD 34.0 billion backlog is conditional on funding and option exercise, and only USD 6.2 billion is funded [CP-1A company and operating model].

5. CACI's contract mix is moving toward more fixed-price work. Fixed-price revenue was 33.2% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 26.7% a year earlier, and cost-plus-fee fell from 60.5% to 52.8% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Mechanism: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Countering evidence: management EBITDA margin rose from 11.7% to 13.3% between the two first quarters [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: earnings variability rises with execution, offset so far by margin gains.

6. CACI's creditor protections cannot be verified. The senior secured instruments (revolver, term loans) total USD 3,364.438 million of floating-rate principal with swaps covering USD 1,400.0 million notional, and USD 1,500.0 million of senior unsecured notes sit beside them [CP-1 financial base]. Covenant levels, definitions, guarantors and baskets are Not supplied; management states compliance with all financial covenants, which is an attributed claim [CP-0; CP-1A governance table]. Credit implication: headroom and default distance cannot be sized, and ranking by entity is not assessable.

7. Subsequent events are mixed. The Board approved a calendar fiscal year on October 20, 2026, so the next report covers a six-month transition period; the litigation judgment was vacated on October 21, 2026, though plaintiffs may seek further review; and fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on October 21, 2026 [CP-1A timeline; CP-1A conflicts]. Credit implication: period comparisons will change and a USD 42 million contingent claim has eased but is not closed.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, revenue is almost entirely federal and backlog-supported, which gives revenue visibility in normal budget conditions [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Second, liquidity is ample: cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,674.389 million against light scheduled amortisation [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Third, cash generation is solid, with operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 775.961 million and cash interest cover of 5.60x on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-supportive on the record: no dividend has been paid, share repurchases were cut and the revolver balance fell from USD 660.0 million to USD 605.0 million in the latest quarter [CP-1A governance table] (Documentary Fact). Fifth, the margin trend is positive, with management EBITDA margin of 13.3% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 11.7% a year earlier [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Management describes its execution as a differentiator, which is Management Language and is not adopted here [CP-1A company and operating model] (Management Language).

Weaknesses. First, leverage is higher after the acquisition, at 3.94x total debt to EBITDA on the latest twelve months against 3.04x at FY2025, and the effect of acquired earnings is unquantified [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact; the overstatement of run-rate leverage is Analyst Interpretation). Second, payer concentration and funding risk: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience and a continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Third, fixed-price work is growing as a share of revenue, which transfers cost-overrun risk to the company [CP-1A company and operating model] (Analyst Interpretation). Fourth, floating-rate exposure: USD 1,964.438 million of floating-rate principal is not covered by swap notional, so higher rates would raise cash interest and lower cover [CP-1 financial base] (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, the company is an active acquirer, with eight acquisitions in three fiscal years and a preliminary purchase price allocation for the latest, so leverage depends on future deal appetite [CP-1A governance table] (Analyst Interpretation). Sixth, the receivable sale program is at its cap with a stated term ending December 18, 2026 [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Seventh, covenant terms, guarantors and ownership are not supplied, which limits the assessment and is not an adverse finding in itself [CP-0; CP-1A company profile] (Insufficient Information).
### Credit assessment and thesis

| Thesis | A federally funded, backlog-supported contractor with ample liquidity and no near-term maturities can service its acquisition debt from cash flow, provided leverage falls and federal funding stays orderly | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same basis |

| Covenant and structure view | Not assessable | Insufficient Information | Insufficient Information | Missing datapoint: executed credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list; it determines headroom and ranking by entity |
### Key credit risks

No new calculation is made in this module. Every figure is carried from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, which hold the inputs, formulas and locators.
